wave: SELF-HOSTING -- close the reverse-direction blind spot the prior generation's own evidence record explicitly recorded as its next step
wave_title: Direct follow-up to the prior generation's own recorded next step: 'extending this same permanent-check pattern to other hand-maintained .atlas/ reference files ... the reverse direction of what this generation checks'. The prior generation verified every donor's evidence path exists; this generation verifies every Technology Genome document that EXISTS is actually referenced by some donor -- catching an orphaned record nobody's evidence trail points back to, a real blind spot even though it currently finds nothing.
priority_classification: self-hosting / verification blindness -- closes a genuine, previously-unchecked gap (no prior check existed in either direction before the immediately preceding generation, and this generation completes the pair) rather than manufacturing a new concern.
empirical_check_before_implementing: before writing any permanent test, ran the equivalent check by hand (comparing the file list of .atlas/genome/technology/*.md against every path referenced in donor-corpus.toml's evidence arrays) to confirm what the new test would actually find -- result: clean, zero orphans and zero dangling references in either direction today. This generation's own value is not a currently-known defect but a durable guard against a FUTURE genome document being written and never linked back to a donor entry, stated explicitly rather than implying a defect was found where none was.

design_decisions.question: Add this as a new, separate test module, or extend the existing donor_corpus_integrity module from the prior generation?
design_decisions.decision: Extended the existing module -- it already has the parsing/loading infrastructure (`load_entries`, the evidence-path extraction) this check reuses directly; a separate module would either duplicate that infrastructure or need to import it, neither better than adding one more #[test] fn to the module that already owns this exact file's parsing.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: Every `.atlas/genome/technology/*.md` file is referenced by at least one donor's evidence array in donor-corpus.toml; a future genome document that is written but never cross-referenced will be caught by this permanent test.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Ran the check by hand first (shell comm/sort against the two file sets) to confirm what the automated version should find, then wrote the automated version and confirmed it agrees (clean, 0 orphans) -- cross-validating the new Rust test against an independent shell-based computation of the same fact, not trusting the new test's own first green result alone.
